stage2CodeEvidence: Core production SQL projection bypasses legacy apply_content_delta and block-only batching; actual SQLx PostgreSQL encoded parameter lengths (including length prefixes) govern shared normal transactions and isolated oversized operations. No per-vault encoded/body queue is introduced.

File completion is invalidated before partial writes, every tag/link/block cleanup effect is budgeted, expected full row counts are verified before complete markers, and the complete revision manifest is checked before publishing a cursor. Retained audit rows are untouched.

Review 75cb546a cancellation fix: acquire owned write coordination before detaching note/deletion work, retain it through SQL/body cleanup, and drain under filesystem coordination before inventory reconciliation and final manifest verification/publication. Detached writers never reacquire the outer filesystem lock; an empty-delta revert cannot publish over a pending pre-invalidation write.

Normalized lowercase plaintext and legacy filename-title projection preserve arbitrary non-overlapping substring counts and title weight 2. PostgreSQL FTS /search remains separate. Raw content/search_text/block-body columns remain blank; lexical plaintext deliberately does not.

Current runtime-policy-derived SQL scope precedes filters/order/pagination. Regex rules use compact Rust policy evaluation; Base fetches referenced properties, scopes link targets before projection/evaluation, and pushes default/numeric ordering into SQL. Heterogeneous/complex Base ordering retains bounded evaluator fallback for exact legacy semantics.

Review 75cb546a query fixes: context authorization/adjacency/hub/similarity/summary lookups share the existing transaction connection, supporting max_connections=1. Base bare date/today/now identifiers select frontmatter properties, while function callees remain builtins. Backlinks and graph BFS use endpoint ID ordering without changing positional exact-note references or hub fanout.

Graph/link/backlink output IDs are complete and output-proportional; counts are scalar SQL. Exact centrality retains ID-only topology, not note metadata/embeddings/frontmatter/bodies. Scalar context candidates rank/page in SQL, and projected token sizes precede selected input hydration.

Exact file leases survive MCP conversion/sanitization/wrapping. Multi-note context and selected search/query-note snippets use a retained operation lease for sequential attested inputs and response processing; full input/parse is discarded before the next acquisition. No wire fields added.

Forthcoming: production embedding-worker ownership/reindex, whole-process RSS/parser/encoding/driver costing, full-stack startup/kill/restart/golden tests and deployment activation. Component tests and synthetic encoded highwaters do not establish these obligations or a numerical singleton/RSS ceiling.
stage2TestEvidence: cargo test -p obts_bridge: 157 passed, 13 explicitly PostgreSQL-dependent checks ignored (59.25s); includes all prior unit checks.

Follow-up explicit PostgreSQL command cargo test -p obts_bridge postgres_ -- --ignored --nocapture passed all 13 checks in 109.23s, including nested subprocess replay. A final four-test focused rerun with strengthened revision/audit assertions passed in 0.46s. All owned bounded_* synthetic databases were removed; the supplied parent database/container was not removed.

Observed default fixture highwaters: normal 128 rows / 18,560 encoded parameter bytes; largest singleton 10,000,040 bytes; two singleton operations including 9 MiB frontmatter. Tiny 3-row/256-byte settings: 3 rows / 203 normal encoded bytes / 4,345 singleton bytes. These fixture values are not parser/RSS ceilings.

The distributed fixture totals 72,194,048 synthetic bytes (~68.85 MiB), not 72 MiB. Private notes project without caller principals, denied Base link targets do not leak, and missing selected FS text does not fall back to lexical storage.

Failure tests cover partially committed link/tag/block work, omitted-tag success-without-row rejection, old cursor/audit preservation, a fresh subprocess replay using only the persistent DB/files, revert cleanup, and actual migration 0020 from a recreated pre-migration complete same-commit schema.

Graph fixture checks 505 links/backlinks/nodes and 1,010 edges, scalar counts, positional hub fanout, negative semantic scores, a late high-ranked non-seed candidate beyond the old cap, one-slot multi-note context with active input highwater 1, response/drop/cancel and source-failure lease release.

FM003 model/check matrix unchanged in this core lane. Earlier 39 FM003 and 52 baseline TLC checks were parent-reported architecture-gate evidence, not rerun implementation conformance proof here. Full-stack abrupt-process-kill, embeddings and measured RSS remain separate evidence.

Final scope also checks source-committed local edit projection failure retains accepted/pending response semantics, and non-object YAML frontmatter preserves key-filter/Base behavior without loading arbitrary values into policy pages.

Regression-first review 75cb546a: postgres_review_cancel_before_invalidation_blocks_noop_revert_publication, postgres_review_context_uses_single_connection_pool, postgres_review_base_bare_builtin_names_are_properties and postgres_review_endpoint_specific_backlink_and_diamond_order all failed before production edits and passed afterward. The cancellation test starts zero-change replay while the old writer is still PG-row-lock blocked, asserts unfinished/not-ready/old-cursor before release, then verifies restored revision inventory, rows and nonempty retained audits. Query tests cover a nonempty scoped/semantic/hub context at pool size one, bare date/today/now and correct function calls, ID-ordered backlinks/diamond BFS, and preserved positional exact-note references.

modelBoundary: Four files, thirteen independent required rows: F1 metadata plus two tags/two links/two blocks; F2 and F4 oversized metadata; finite body sizes are independent of encoded row sizes. Fixture sizes are not a parser expansion ratio.

Ordered file acquisition and per-file row enqueue reduce interleavings; two simultaneous bodies, normal byte pressure, isolated singleton execution/cleanup and cancellation during singleton ownership are explicitly reached.

One interrupted target is replayed after partial commits with durable rows retained; a healthy run separately reaches cursor 3 from cursor 1. Superseded/deleted-row cleanup is an abstract completion action, not a proof of production SQL deletion/revert semantics.

Oversized-starvation disables singleton admission while keeping supported inputs and fair normal actions: TLC must violate the sole configured completion property. It is a liveness counterexample, not a made-up rejection invariant.

SingletonPermitClean/SingletonOwned model shared ownership through commit then cleanup; concrete parser/driver disposal, SQL/compiler, API format/order and lexical equivalence are executable-test obligations, not TLA proofs.
